source.title: Fractional moment-preserving initialization schemes for training fully-connected neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares initialization schemes and reports training accuracy during early training, bearing on initialization-dependent training progress. It does not measure convergence to near-zero error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy for several initializations on MNIST and CIFAR-10; these are included because training accuracy measures training classification error. Cited findings from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares SGD training progress under different initializations, testing V4's training-speed component. Its short training runs do not test V1's eventual near-zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: fractional-moment initialization can improve initial training progress. The paper also develops moment-preservation and output-distribution theory; it does not establish eventual near-zero training error or greater maximum trainable depth.
record.recipe_differences: Uses i.i.d. Gaussian weights with variance adjusted to preserve a chosen fractional moment of layer outputs, compared with Xavier, Kaiming and random walk initializations. Reports short training runs rather than convergence tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported early training accuracy varies by initialization, activation and dataset; the proposed initialization is not uniformly higher than every comparator in the listed means.

fits_no_version.finding: Fractional-moment preservation changes output-norm distributions and gradient-noise tails. Theorem 14 also shows that moment preservation can coexist with outputs tending to zero at increasing depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving an output moment does not by itself ensure nonvanishing typical signals; initialization can alter signal distributions and gradient-noise tails.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2021, PMLR Volume 130
record.problems: Training results cover only early epochs; several datasets and architectures have small sample counts (10 or 20 runs). Some comparisons show only small gains over Kaiming initialization. The paper does not report the claimed long-run near-zero training error.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible training-accuracy table rows were left out. The figures also plot additional curves, but exact plotted values are not stated in the text and are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Eventual zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs; corrupted or random labels; CIFAR-100; effects of model size, stopping time and regularization.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep tanh networks and Fixup.
Maximum trainable depth, controlled training comparisons across depths, tanh networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training and divergence thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance and normalization-free Fixup training.

missing.what: Actual linear MNIST training-accuracy rows: Xavier 85.71%, Randwalk 86.29%, Kaiming 85.53%, and s=1 86.16%, over 20 runs in a 30-layer width-64 network. These are missing because R16–R18 contain Figure 11's CIFAR-10 values instead.
missing.locator: Appendix O.2, Figure 13 and accompanying table

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Remove the V1 verdict: an untested convergence endpoint is not a scope limitation. Small gains over Kaiming do not alone limit V4, which does not claim fractional-moment initialization must outperform Kaiming. Figure-only training curves were already declared omitted in rows_left_out. Accuracy standard deviations are reproduced as printed, but their scale relative to percentage means is ambiguous.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convergence to zero or near-zero training error after sufficiently long training, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, or the claimed large convolutional-network setting. Reports early-stage training accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
Does not compare orthogonal and Gaussian weights, test trainable depth, or evaluate 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
